Quantum:2cab16e0b965.title: Sorbonne Université and Qubit Pharmaceuticals Introduce VULCAN Hybrid Framework for Scalable Quantum Chemistry
Quantum:2cab16e0b965.summary: Sorbonne Université and Qubit Pharmaceuticals developed VULCAN, a hybrid quantum-classical framework for quantum chemistry that overcomes limitations of ADAPT-VQE.
Quantum:2cab16e0b965.text: Sorbonne Université and Qubit Pharmaceuticals developed VULCAN, a hybrid quantum-classical framework for quantum chemistry that overcomes limitations of ADAPT-VQE. VULCAN achieves chemical accuracy with significantly fewer quantum resources by employing techniques like dynamic Lie-algebraic operator pool generation, state-overlap circuit compression, and adaptive-subspace projection. Benchmarks show VULCAN outperforms batched ADAPT-VQE in terms of measurement cost and ability to reach chemical accuracy on complex molecules.

Quantum:d3ef89c20500.summary: Researchers from Qubit Pharmaceuticals and Sorbonne Université have developed a new method for quantum chemistry, introducing a polynomial-scaling algebraic framework to construct and verify Minimal Complete Pools (MCPs) for variational quantum eigensolvers (VQE).
Quantum:d3ef89c20500.text: Researchers from Qubit Pharmaceuticals and Sorbonne Université have developed a new method for quantum chemistry, introducing a polynomial-scaling algebraic framework to construct and verify Minimal Complete Pools (MCPs) for variational quantum eigensolvers (VQE). This approach significantly reduces computational overhead, as demonstrated by GPU-accelerated benchmarks on the Jean Zay supercomputer. The team has open-sourced their C++ and CUDA routines for MCP verification on GitHub.

Quantum:12e7e4713e23.text: Researchers from Qubit Pharmaceuticals, Sorbonne Université, and Q-CTRL successfully demonstrated 3D protein hydration-site prediction on IBM Heron quantum processors, utilizing up to 123 qubits to identify optimal water placements in drug-target proteins. Their quantum approach outperformed classical methods in certain scenarios, finding lower-energy solutions and achieving higher optimal sampling probabilities. This research paves the way for practical computer-aided drug discovery, with projections indicating utility with approximately 900 qubits.

Quantum:cc8c69bc5525.title: QuEra, Harvard, and UMD Researchers Develop Polynomial-Time Classical Benchmarking for Non-Clifford Fault-Tolerant Circuits
Quantum:cc8c69bc5525.summary: Researchers developed a polynomial-time Monte Carlo method for benchmarking fault-tolerant non-Clifford quantum circuits, which are essential for universal quantum computation.
Quantum:cc8c69bc5525.text: Researchers developed a polynomial-time Monte Carlo method for benchmarking fault-tolerant non-Clifford quantum circuits, which are essential for universal quantum computation. This method efficiently simulates complex circuits and evaluates logical fidelity by backpropagating Pauli faults and reducing errors to Clifford operators. They demonstrated its effectiveness on circuits up to 256 physical qubits and various magic-state factory designs, finding that a shared ancilla block significantly improves efficiency.

Policy:ea0cd6b18305.summary: Outages happen, but we deserve a resilient internet where no one outage at one company can put people at risk and disrupt the global economy.
Policy:ea0cd6b18305.text: Outages happen, but we deserve a resilient internet where no one outage at one company can put people at risk and disrupt the global economy. We can only get there by addressing an over-reliance on a few cloud monopolists through effective antitrust laws and interoperability requirements. Service outages, like we’ve seen recently at Microsoft , Apple *, banks , courts , airlines , and elsewhere, can be more than an annoying hurdle. Losing a vital service due to an error can cause the same impacts as a government-ordered internet shutdown—people losing access to vital information and lines of communication. As usual, the greatest harms are faced by people on the margins globally. There’s not much hope in companies out-nerding these issues either. Technical errors will always exist, whether it’s a bug , negligence from an administrator, or a malicious attack. The problem is an over-reliance on any one company or system when these inevitable outages occur. AI:a320002a9775.title: Adding One More Agent: How AI Team Size and Formation Shape Productivity and Diversity in Human-AI Brainstorming Teams
AI:a320002a9775.summary: Generative AI has improved individual productivity, but whether adding a plurality of AI partners helps or hurts remains open.
AI:a320002a9775.text: Generative AI has improved individual productivity, but whether adding a plurality of AI partners helps or hurts remains open. We crossed AI partnership (one versus two) with behavioral formation (calibrated to average human behavior versus customized by the participant) in a brainstorming experiment ($N$=168) with human-human dyads as reference. Two-AI rooms posted more ideas to the shared board, but human-authored ideas dropped substantially. With one AI partner, formation mattered: humans paired with an average-calibrated AI posted more than any other condition. With two, this effect vanished. Humans continued talking but converted fewer ideas into board posts. AI social talk predicted more human posts, while AI posting volume predicted fewer. AI presence increased global diversity of human-authored ideas, but only a second AI increased within-session differentiation. The number of AI partners and their formation can reshape what the human contributes; single-agent results do not generalize to multi-agent teams.

Quantum:e3f6064b25d8.text: Recent works have proposed semi-device-independent frameworks to certify non-stabilizerness, but the complexity of the stabilizer polytope makes these methods infeasible beyond a few qubits. In this work, we address this limitation by moving to partially characterized measurements in the context of worst-case random access codes. We first establish a simple condition, which we term the stabilizer pigeonhole criterion, that certifies non-stabilizerness in $m$-qubit pure states, and show how it can be applied to reduced states. Quantum:8836e4b95686.title: Improved Digitization Bounds for U(1) Lattice Gauge Theory via Semiclassical Analysis
Quantum:8836e4b95686.summary: Simulating lattice gauge theories on a digital quantum computer or using tensor network methods requires a finite-dimensional approximation of the gauge field, a process often called digitization.
Quantum:8836e4b95686.text: Simulating lattice gauge theories on a digital quantum computer or using tensor network methods requires a finite-dimensional approximation of the gauge field, a process often called digitization. Controlling the resulting error is essential for assessing the accuracy and resource requirements of these simulations. In this work, we derive a digitization error bound for low-lying eigenstates of the Kogut--Susskind Hamiltonian for pure U(1) gauge theory and translate it into a bound on time-evolution error. Compared with existing bounds, our result achieves exponentially improved dependence on the inverse lattice spacing $1/a$ and evolution time $T$, together with improved dependence on the inverse coupling $1/g$. The key idea is to identify a small parameter in the Kogut--Susskind Hamiltonian and apply tools from semiclassical analysis. Specifically, we adapt Agmon's method to establish exponential decay of the error with the truncation threshold. These results sharpen estimates of the local Hilbert space dimension and qubit resources needed to simulate gauge theories near the continuum limit, at weak coupling, and over long times.

Telecommunications:5e777eb1b934.text: Mobile robots in industrial workspaces must react to people that their onboard sensors cannot yet observe. Communication infrastructure can fill part of this gap by acting as a sensor, but its observations differ from camera and LiDAR evidence in meaning, spatial support, and rate. We present a live robotic Digital Twin (DT) that integrates heterogeneous sensing branches, a commodity 60-GHz link, joint Wi-Fi/5G sensing, a fixed camera, and robot-borne LiDAR, as spatially grounded observations with explicit freshness, and that uses the robot's live pose and heading to decide whether evidence lies on the path the robot is about to sweep. Telecommunications:cb1986e4a37c.title: TITAN: DRL-Based Dynamic Scheduling and Resource Allocation for Tactile Internet
Telecommunications:cb1986e4a37c.summary: Tactile Internet (TI) applications require ultra-reliable, low-latency tactile communication alongside video traffic. However, tactile Quality of Service (QoS) requirements vary with the interaction context, making fixed resource allocation inefficient.
Telecommunications:cb1986e4a37c.text: Tactile Internet (TI) applications require ultra-reliable, low-latency tactile communication alongside video traffic. However, tactile Quality of Service (QoS) requirements vary with the interaction context, making fixed resource allocation inefficient. In this paper, we propose TITAN (Two-Timescale Integrated Tactile Internet over 5G Access Networks), a dynamic scheduling and resource allocation (SRA) scheme. TITAN receives time-varying tactile QoS profiles from a higher-layer module and adapts SRA to the current QoS profile and network state. A deep reinforcement learning-based agent splits the available network bandwidth between tactile and video streams at a slow timescale, while a fast-timescale scheduler allocates resource blocks among active user equipment. Through simulations, we show that TITAN simultaneously satisfies both tactile and video QoS targets and achieves a performance gain of 7.64 percentage points (pp) in the joint satisfaction rate over the best-performing static SRA baseline.
